Theme

snare noun

also noose, trap, springe, gin

classical

Caes. BG 7.22: laqueīs falcēs āvertēbant (Lewis & Short)
Sall. Jug. 94: saxa laqueīs vinciēbat (Lewis & Short)
Plaut. Truc. 2.4.41 (Lewis & Short)

laqueus, laqueī m.

noun, second declension

a noose, a snare

Other words

  • pedica, pedicae f. — a snare for the feet, a springe

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Liv. 21.36 (Lewis & Short); Verg. G. 1.307: tunc gruibus pedicās et rētia pōnere cervīs (Lewis & Short)

    From pēs.

Examples

  • tum laqueīs captāre ferās et fallere viscō inventum

    then men found out how to catch wild beasts in snares and trick birds with limeVerg. G. 1.139–140

  • tum gruibus pedicās et rētia pōnere cervīs

    then is the time to set snares for cranes and nets for deerVerg. G. 1.307

See also hunt, net, mistletoe, wild.

SourcesLewis & Short: laqueus · Lewis & Short: pedica

Vergil, Georgica 1.139–140, 1.307.
